1 · The prompts

Vibe-coding prompts — Phase 2: integration under uncertainty

Tool: Claude Code (model: Claude Opus 5.5), run inside this repository.

There are two layers of prompt:

  • Prompt 0 is the request exactly as it was typed to the assistant.
  • Prompts 1–11 are the component prompts that request was broken into. Each one is self-contained: pasting it into a coding assistant, together with the repository, should regenerate the corresponding module. They are listed in the order the code was generated.

The code as it stood straight after generation, before anything was run, is frozen in vibe_coding/generated_v0/. Every change made after that point is listed in CHANGES.md and highlighted line by line in the diff report (python vibe_coding/make_diff_report.py, then open dashboard/vibe/index.html).

Prompt 0 — the request

  • Given a scanned image of a car registration, find out all vehicles approximately matching with this nosy car plate and vice-versa.   • Cleansed the recorded data w.r.t. the image data and other contextual information so that there are no anomalies (including the noise) in the recorded data. (5)
  • Show me the prompt (for vibe coding), generated code and highlights the changes you have made in the generated code. (5)

Prompt 1 — dataset

Extend the four existing silos (DB1 retail POS, DB2 distributor ledger, DB3 manufacturer registry, DB4 ministry) with a deterministic synthetic dataset big enough to defend integration under uncertainty. Keep the 20 curated phase-1 items and their verdicts unchanged. Add ~6 manufacturers, ~35 molecules with invented brand names, 2–4 consecutive batches per SKU (consecutive batch numbers so many codes are one edit apart), ~30 pharmacies across 9 Indian cities plus unlicensed kiosks, shipments by authorised distributors, and checkout scans at the pharmacies that actually received each batch. Capture channel matters: barcode/QR reads are almost always right, hand entry and camera (OCR) reads are not. Inject every kind of defect with a typed noise channel: OCR glyph confusion, keyboard slips, transpositions, deletions, insertions, truncation, format noise, a real-but-wrong sibling code; exact and near duplicate rows; master-data duplicates (a batch registered twice, a pharmacy registered twice with its licence formatted differently); manufacturer conflicts and missing values in DB2; unit errors in prices; ambiguous DD/MM dates; citizen complaints with misspelt brands, codes only in the free text, and complaints filed twice. Add counterfeits: codes one or two edits from real ones and fabricated codes, shipped by ghost distributors to kiosks and sometimes to licensed pharmacies, sold at 30–60% of MRP, complained about, and blacklisted (one blacklist entry with formatting noise). For camera captures store the OCR text of the label in a new purchase_events.label_text column, and the photo path in label_image. Write the ground truth for every record to data/generated/ground_truth.json, which the matcher must never read.

Prompt 2 — string metrics and noise channel

Implement, without third-party packages: Levenshtein, Damerau-Levenshtein (optimal string alignment), Jaro-Winkler, padded q-gram Jaccard and American Soundex, each with a [0,1] similarity. Separately implement a typed noise channel (ocr, keyboard, transpose, delete, insert, format, truncate, mixed) with per-capture-channel profiles, seeded by a random.Random, used both to generate the dataset and to augment the benchmark.

Prompt 3 — learned noisy-channel distance for codes

Write a weighted OSA edit distance for printed codes: substitution cost depends on the pair of characters, transposition 0.6, separator insertion/deletion 0.1, a doubled keystroke 0.5, other indels 1.0, banded for speed. Start from a prior built from glyph-shape classes (O/0, I/1/L, S/5, B/8, Z/2, G/6 …) and learn substitution costs from (observed, true) training pairs via an alignment backtrace. Expose distance, similarity, fit, top_confusions, serialisation, and a discretisation of distance into agreement levels L0–L4.

Prompt 4 — standardisation

Deterministic format canonicalisation that never changes a character: pack codes to MED-FAMILY-NNN (case, spacing, separators, country prefix, GS1 digital-link serial), dates from ISO, DD/MM/YYYY, DD-Mon-YYYY, Mon DD YYYY (report both readings of an ambiguous DD/MM date), currency aliases to INR, vendor-id spellings to VND-NNN, licence keys, brand and strength keys, and a tolerant parser for OCR label text (brand, strength, batch, expiry month, MRP, code) that survives digits read as letters.

Prompt 5 — live context

A read-only snapshot of the silos used as matching evidence: registered products, vendors, distributors, manufacturer→distributor authorisations, custody (which product was shipped to which pharmacy, when), and a bigram blocking index on confusion-folded codes. Rebuild it automatically whenever any SQLite file changes so inserts, updates and deletes are visible to the next request. Support alias maps (duplicate product → survivor, duplicate pharmacy → survivor). Custody from damaged DB2 serials may only come from confident links.

Prompt 6 — probabilistic linkage

Implement Fellegi–Sunter record linkage for one noisy record against the registry: block, build a comparison vector per candidate (code level by capture channel; for checkouts: custody, price vs MRP, date consistency, and label brand/strength/batch/expiry/MRP; for shipments: manufacturer, distributor authorisation, dispatch date; for complaints: brand and shop mentioned in the text), weight each value by log2(m/u), and normalise into a posterior over the candidates and a null hypothesis "this code belongs to no registered product" with prior π0 per source. Decide EXACT / AUTO_LINK / REVIEW / NO_MATCH / VALID_BUT_WRONG. Provide the reverse lookup (every record that approximately refers to a product), plain-English explanations, and a per-query comparison of every string metric.

Prompt 7 — cleanser

Scan all four silos and produce issues with category, decision (AUTO, REVIEW, RETAIN), confidence, method, explanation and the exact row changes: format mismatches, noisy and valid-but-wrong identifiers, duplicate rows (POS retry, ERP re-import, complaint filed twice — close as duplicate, never delete a citizen's complaint), master-data duplicates with survivorship and re-pointing of references, cross-source conflicts resolved by source authority (DB3 owns who made a product) or annotated when neither source outranks the other, missing values imputed only when another silo determines them, unit-error outliers, and counterfeit codes quarantined, never rewritten into a real product. Apply with a lineage log (old value, new value, deleted-row snapshot) so any run can be undone; let a reviewer accept, pick another candidate or reject. Keep the DB1 JSON document mirror in sync.

Prompt 8 — training and benchmark

Split the labelled records 50/50 by record (a record and its re-corrupted copies on the same side). On the training half fit the confusion costs, the Fellegi–Sunter m/u tables and π0, and tune the thresholds for maximum automation subject to 99.5% auto-link precision. On the held-out half compare Levenshtein, Damerau-Levenshtein, Jaro-Winkler, bigram Jaccard, Soundex, the learned distance alone, Fellegi–Sunter on the code only, and Fellegi–Sunter with context: top-1 (all and damaged only), recall@5, MRR, link precision/recall/F1, the share of counterfeit codes linked to a real product, review rate, per-noise-kind accuracy, blocking completeness, and a separate brand-name benchmark. Save the model and the results as JSON.

Prompt 9 — API and wiring

Add /api/v1/uncertainty/* (match, compare, reverse, catalog, samples, scan, apply, decide, undo, lineage, benchmark, train) in one module that both nodes delegate to. After every explorer INSERT/UPDATE on purchase_events, distribution_batches or complaints, return the matcher's reading of the written row in the same response, and re-sync the DB1 mirror after any DB1 write. Fix FEDERATED_INSERT (RUNNING.md 5.1) so its writes satisfy the DB2/DB1 constraints and its success reflects the results.

Prompt 10 — dashboard

A new page dashboard/uncertainty.html in the existing design system: match a noisy code or a label photo (in-browser OCR with Tesseract.js, falling back to the recorded OCR text), ranked candidates with evidence chips and posteriors, per-metric comparison; reverse lookup; the benchmark with justification drawn from the numbers; scan/apply/review/undo; lineage; insert/modify/delete test cards that write through the explorer endpoint and show the answer before and after; a link to this vibe-coding report. Link it from the other pages' navs.

Prompt 11 — label images

Render the photographed pack label for each camera-captured checkout from the product's registered data (what is really printed), then damage it like a counter camera would: tilt, blur, sensor noise, glare, JPEG compression. Pillow optional; skip cleanly without it.

2 · What was changed after generation, and why

Changes made to the generated code

vibe_coding/generated_v0/ holds every new or touched file exactly as the assistant first wrote it, before a single line was run (snapshot taken 2026-10-20 01:06). Everything below was changed afterwards, because running, testing or reviewing the code showed it was wrong. Each entry says what was observed, what was changed, and where. The diff report highlights every one of these lines.

Found by running the benchmark

1. Console crash on Windows. train.py printed → in the results table; the Windows console (cp1252) cannot encode it and the run died after 200 s of work. → ASCII header (fake->real). train.py

2. Learned substitution costs were miscalibrated. With the first formula, 1 − 0.85 · share, the cheapest learned pairs were C→G and H→N (0.33), while the 0/O confusion, the most common OCR error in the data, did not even reach the ten cheapest (all ≤ 0.40). That made it dearer than its 0.25 shape prior. A character with several genuine confusions (0 is read as O, D, Q, 8) splits its share among them, so each one looked rare. → Cost from the likelihood ratio against a random slip: 1 − log(p/p0)/log(1/p0), p0 = 1/36. A printed 0 read as O now costs 0.16. confusion.py

3. Auto-link threshold tuned down to 0.5. Grid search found 0.5 still met 99.5% precision on the synthetic training split. Rewriting a medicine record on a coin flip is not acceptable when the training data is synthetic. → Policy floors: auto-link ≥ 0.90, no-match ≥ 0.80. train.py

4. Training ignored duplicate pharmacy records. Sales booked under VND-036 (Apollo Bandra registered a second time) got custody "same city" instead of "shipped to this pharmacy", so a sibling batch won (MED-FVRLE-785 chosen for …-786). The cleanser used vendor aliases, training did not. → Duplicate detection made static and shared (duplicate_aliases), training builds its context with both alias maps. cleanser.py, train.py

5. A real-but-wrong code was always accepted. MED-MTPRE-696 sold before batch 696 was even manufactured had 99.9% of the probability on its siblings, but no single sibling reached 0.6, so the rule kept the wrong code. → VALID_BUT_WRONG when the probability mass on other registered products is ≥ 0.6; one shared is_auto() policy for the cleanser and the evaluation (they had used different definitions of "automatic"). linkage.py, cleanser.py

6. Shipments could not separate sibling batches. 203 of the 320 genuine records left for review were DB2 shipments: consecutive batches share maker, carrier and dates, so only the code discriminated. → Cross-silo evidence: was this batch later scanned by barcode at the destination pharmacy (DB1 → DB2, scanner reads only, so no circular fuzzy link); destination licence; dispatch lag after manufacture. Together with 7, held-out link recall rose from 88% to 94% at 99.9% precision. context.py, linkage.py

7. The no-match target treated both mistakes as equally bad. Requiring 97% precision for "no product" pushed its threshold to 0.995 and left every counterfeit in review. A wrong link destroys counterfeit evidence; a wrong quarantine is an annotation a reviewer can lift. → 90% target for no-match, 99.5% kept for links. On the held-out split every counterfeit code is now called "no registered product" outright (100%), none is linked to a real product. train.py

8. Smoothing artefact. DB2 date=expired got +2.08 bits although it was never observed in either class: Laplace smoothing with very different denominators turns "never seen" into evidence for a match. → Smoothing toward the prior m/u instead (now −0.66). train.py

9. Benchmark speed. Exact top-k pruning: candidates visited in bigram order, edit-distance DP abandoned once it cannot beat the k-th best. The bound uses the last two DP rows because an OSA transposition jumps from row i−2 to row i. Verified identical to exhaustive scoring on 60 codes. similarity.py, confusion.py, train.py

Found by running the cleanser

10. A counterfeit blacklist entry was steered toward a real product. BL-G02 stored med cprvn 590 (a fake code with formatting noise). The review suggestion was MED-CPRVN-580, a genuine product; accepting it would blacklist a real medicine and leave the fake un-vetoed. → Regulatory references (ministry_blacklist, public_alerts, lab_reports) are always canonicalised (format only, so the V2 veto finds them) and never re-pointed at a registered product without a person. After cleansing, MED-CPRVN-590 now triggers the V2 blacklist veto. cleanser.py

11. Reviewers had no "this is a fake" option. → Third decision: quarantine as counterfeit evidence. Quarantined rows are not re-reported. Annotations are appended to existing notes (_append_note) instead of overwriting, e.g. a "units damaged in transit" note. cleanser.py, uncertainty.js

12. Apply and undo hardening. Apply runs to a fixpoint (a fixed code can reveal a duplicate). Undo refuses to revert a run while a later run that touched the same rows is still applied, because it would silently overwrite the later change. cleanser.py

13a. Duplicates hidden behind a typo. Scored against ground truth, the duplicate detector found 49 of 56 injected duplicates (no false positives). The 7 it missed were re-keyed: a POS retry typed again with a typo, a complaint refiled with a different damaged code. Grouping on the resolved product never brought them together. → The neighbouring record is itself the evidence: same till, price and quantity within a minute, and codes a small learned distance apart; for complaints, the same person within three days with near-identical codes or a description that repeats the earlier one. Now 56 of 56, still no false positives. cleanser.py

Found through the API and the browser

13. A label photo without a readable code found nothing. Candidates came only from the code, and an absent code was scored as "far from every product". → The label's brand and damaged batch number propose candidates; the code feature is omitted when there is no code. Explanations name the candidate their evidence describes. linkage.py

14. The match endpoint showed duplicate master records. MED-CALCI-218 (a second registration of a Calcivane batch) appeared as a candidate while the cleanser treated it as an alias. → live_matcher() gives every endpoint the same alias-aware view as a scan. cleanser.py, http_api.py

15. Page text that overclaimed. The names note said Jaro-Winkler was chosen because typos fall late in a word; the benchmark shows Damerau-Levenshtein marginally ahead (99.9% vs 99.6%) and the noise is position-uniform. The counterfeit card named the wrong lookalikes. → Both now match the measured data. uncertainty.js, uncertainty.html

16. Training on cleansed data went unreported. → The benchmark records how many cleansing changes were applied and the page warns. train.py, uncertainty.js

Phase-1 files changed outside the snapshot

  • scripts/run_cluster.py: --stop used ps and SIGKILL, neither of which exists on Windows; it now uses PowerShell/CIM and taskkill there.
  • create_databases.py, data/seed_db1..4.py: honour ASALI_DB_DIR so the test suite builds in a temporary directory.

665        quantity, seconds apart, and a code a small learned distance from the

213    held, a distance computation is abandoned as soon as it cannot beat the k-th

<main>

<!-- ========================= INTRO ========================= -->
<section class="shell section-tight" style="padding-bottom:12px;">
  <div class="row-wrap gap-4 between">
    <div style="max-width:60ch;">
      <p class="eyebrow eyebrow-lime">Phase 2 · Integration under uncertainty</p>
      <h1 class="display display-lg" style="margin-top:10px;">The same pack, <span class="hl-lime">recorded four ways</span></h1>
    </div>
    <p class="lede" style="max-width:48ch;">
      A pharmacist types a smudged serial. A phone camera reads a label through glare. A clerk re-keys a
      dispatch note; a citizen types a code into a complaint form. This page links those imperfect
      records back to the registry, cleanses the silos, and keeps every counterfeit signal intact.
    </p>
  </div>
  <div class="bento" style="gap:12px; margin-top:22px;" id="introStats">
    <div class="col-3"><div class="card card-inset card-pad-sm"><p class="stat-num" id="statProducts">—</p><p class="xsmall faint">Registered products (DB3)</p></div></div>
    <div class="col-3"><div class="card card-inset card-pad-sm"><p class="stat-num" id="statVendors">—</p><p class="xsmall faint">Pharmacies (DB1)</p></div></div>
    <div class="col-3"><div class="card card-inset card-pad-sm"><p class="stat-num" id="statModel">—</p><p class="xsmall faint">Linkage model</p></div></div>
    <div class="col-3"><div class="card card-inset card-pad-sm"><p class="stat-num" id="statThreshold">—</p><p class="xsmall faint">Auto-link threshold</p></div></div>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- ========================= 1. MATCH ========================= -->
<section class="shell section-tight" id="match">
  <div class="stack gap-4">
    <div>
      <p class="eyebrow">1 · Approximate match</p>
      <h2 class="display display-md" style="margin-top:8px;">Which registered products could this be?</h2>
      <p class="muted small" style="margin-top:8px; max-width:80ch;">
        Give a noisy code, a photo of the label, or both. Every registered product close enough to be a
        candidate is listed with the evidence for and against it, and with an explicit probability that the
        code belongs to <em>no</em> registered product, which is what a counterfeit looks like.
      </p>
    </div>

    <div class="u-grid">
      <!-- input -->
      <div class="card card-pad-lg">
        <div class="row-wrap gap-2">
          <button class="pill-btn is-active" data-demo="ciplox">Smudged Ciplox, typed</button>
          <button class="pill-btn" data-demo="novamox">Novamox, read by camera</button>
          <button class="pill-btn" data-demo="fake">Counterfeit near-miss</button>
          <button class="pill-btn" data-demo="random">Random noisy record</button>
        </div>

        <label class="eyebrow u-field-label" for="mCode">Scanned or typed code</label>
        <input id="mCode" class="field mono" spellcheck="false" placeholder="e.g. MED-ASAL1-OO7">

        <div class="u-two">
          <div>
            <label class="eyebrow u-field-label" for="mChannel">Captured by</label>
            <select id="mChannel" class="field field-sm u-select">
              <option value="manual">Typed by hand</option>
              <option value="ocr">Camera / OCR of the label</option>
              <option value="scan">Barcode / QR scanner</option>
            </select>
          </div>
          <div>
            <label class="eyebrow u-field-label" for="mVendor">Sold at (context)</label>
            <select id="mVendor" class="field field-sm u-select"><option value="">— unknown —</option></select>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="u-three">
          <div>
            <label class="eyebrow u-field-label" for="mPrice">Price paid (Rs)</label>
            <input id="mPrice" class="field field-sm" inputmode="decimal" placeholder="95">
          </div>
          <div>
            <label class="eyebrow u-field-label" for="mQty">Quantity</label>
            <input id="mQty" class="field field-sm" inputmode="numeric" placeholder="1">
          </div>
          <div>
            <label class="eyebrow u-field-label" for="mDate">Sale date</label>
            <input id="mDate" class="field field-sm" placeholder="2025-06-02 11:20">
          </div>
        </div>

        <hr class="divider-dashed" style="margin-block:18px 4px;">
        <p class="eyebrow u-field-label">Scanned image of the pack (optional)</p>
        <div class="u-two">
          <select id="mSample" class="field field-sm u-select"><option value="">Pick a captured pack…</option></select>
          <label class="btn btn-ghost btn-sm" style="justify-content:center;">
            Upload a photo
            <input id="mUpload" type="file" accept="image/*" class="hidden">
          </label>
        </div>
        <img id="mPreview" class="u-preview hidden" alt="Selected label image" style="margin-top:10px;">
        <div class="row-wrap gap-2" style="margin-top:10px;">
          <button class="btn btn-outline btn-sm" id="btnOcr" disabled>Read image with OCR</button>
          <span class="u-muted-note" id="ocrStatus">OCR runs in the browser (Tesseract.js, first use downloads ~10 MB).</span>
        </div>
        <label class="eyebrow u-field-label" for="mLabel">Text read off the label</label>
        <textarea id="mLabel" class="textarea" rows="3" style="width:100%; min-height:72px; padding:10px;" spellcheck="false" placeholder="NOVAMOX 500MG | Amoxycillin | B.No. BATCH-A001 | EXP 01/2027 | MRP Rs.115.00 | MED-ASALI-0O1"></textarea>

        <button class="btn btn-primary full" style="margin-top:16px;" id="btnMatch">Find matching products</button>
      </div>

      <!-- results -->
      <div class="card card-pad-lg">
        <div id="matchResult"><p class="muted small">Run a match to see the candidates.</p></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- ========================= 2. REVERSE ========================= -->
<section class="shell section-tight" id="reverse">
  <div class="stack gap-4">
    <div>
      <p class="eyebrow">2 · And the other way round</p>
      <h2 class="display display-md" style="margin-top:8px;">Every record that is really about this product</h2>
      <p class="muted small" style="margin-top:8px; max-width:80ch;">
        Pick a registered product. Every checkout, shipment, complaint and regulatory entry that
        approximately refers to it is found across DB1, DB2 and DB4, including the ones whose stored code is damaged.
      </p>
    </div>
    <div class="card card-pad-lg">
      <div class="row-wrap gap-2">
        <input id="rUid" class="field field-sm mono" list="productList" placeholder="MED-ASALI-007" style="max-width:280px;" spellcheck="false">
        <datalist id="productList"></datalist>
        <button class="btn btn-primary btn-sm" id="btnReverse">Find its records</button>
        <span class="u-muted-note">Try MED-ASALI-001, or any code from the registry.</span>
      </div>
      <div id="reverseResult" style="margin-top:16px;"></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- ========================= 3. ALGORITHMS ========================= -->
<section class="shell section-tight" id="algorithms">
  <div class="stack gap-4">
    <div class="row-wrap gap-4 between">
      <div>
        <p class="eyebrow">3 · Justification</p>
        <h2 class="display display-md" style="margin-top:8px;">Why this algorithm, measured</h2>
      </div>
      <div class="row-wrap gap-2">
        <span class="u-muted-note" id="trainStatus"></span>
        <button class="btn btn-outline btn-sm" id="btnRetrain">Refit and re-run benchmark</button>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div id="benchResult"><div class="card card-pad-lg"><p class="muted small">Loading the benchmark…</p></div></div>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- ========================= 4. CLEANSE ========================= -->
<section class="shell section-tight" id="cleanse">
  <div class="stack gap-4">
    <div class="row-wrap gap-4 between">
      <div style="max-width:70ch;">
        <p class="eyebrow">4 · Cleansing</p>
        <h2 class="display display-md" style="margin-top:8px;">Scan the silos, fix what is safe, ask about the rest</h2>
        <p class="muted small" style="margin-top:8px;">
          Each anomaly gets a proposed fix, a confidence and a reason. Automatic fixes are deterministic or above the
          link threshold; uncertain ones wait for a person; codes that belong to no product are quarantined, never rewritten.
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="row-wrap gap-2">
        <button class="btn btn-outline btn-sm" id="btnScan">Scan all silos</button>
        <button class="btn btn-primary btn-sm" id="btnApply" disabled>Apply automatic fixes</button>
      </div>
    </div>
    <p class="u-muted-note" id="scanStatus">Not scanned yet.</p>
    <div class="bento" style="gap:10px;" id="scanTiles"></div>
    <div id="applyResult"></div>
    <div class="card card-pad-lg">
      <div class="row-wrap gap-2 between" style="margin-bottom:12px;">
        <div class="row-wrap gap-2">
          <select id="fDecision" class="field field-sm u-select" style="width:auto;">
            <option value="open">Open issues</option>
            <option value="AUTO">Automatic</option>
            <option value="REVIEW">Needs review</option>
            <option value="RETAIN">Quarantined</option>
            <option value="DISMISSED">Dismissed</option>
            <option value="all">Everything</option>
          </select>
          <select id="fCategory" class="field field-sm u-select" style="width:auto;"><option value="">All categories</option></select>
          <input id="fSearch" class="field field-sm" placeholder="Filter by code or id" style="width:200px;" spellcheck="false">
        </div>
        <span class="u-muted-note" id="issueCount"></span>
      </div>
      <div class="table-wrap u-scroll">
        <table class="data"><thead><tr>
          <th>Category</th><th>Where</th><th>Recorded</th><th>Proposed</th><th>Confidence</th><th>Decision</th><th>Why</th>
        </tr></thead><tbody id="issueRows"><tr><td colspan="7" class="muted">Run a scan.</td></tr></tbody></table>
      </div>
      <div class="row-wrap gap-2" style="margin-top:12px; justify-content:flex-end;">
        <button class="btn btn-ghost btn-sm" id="btnPrev">Previous</button>
        <span class="u-muted-note" id="pageInfo"></span>
        <button class="btn btn-ghost btn-sm" id="btnNext">Next</button>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- ========================= 5. LINEAGE ========================= -->
<section class="shell section-tight" id="lineage">
  <div class="stack gap-4">
    <div class="row-wrap gap-4 between">
      <div>
        <p class="eyebrow">5 · Lineage</p>
        <h2 class="display display-md" style="margin-top:8px;">Every change, and how to take it back</h2>
      </div>
      <button class="btn btn-outline btn-sm" id="btnLineage">Refresh</button>
    </div>
    <div class="card card-pad-lg" id="lineageResult"><p class="muted small">Nothing applied yet.</p></div>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- ========================= 6. TEST ========================= -->
<section class="shell section-tight" id="test">
  <div class="stack gap-4">
    <div>
      <p class="eyebrow">6 · Insert, modify, delete</p>
      <h2 class="display display-md" style="margin-top:8px;">Change the data and watch the answer change</h2>
      <p class="muted small" style="margin-top:8px; max-width:80ch;">
        Each test writes through the same explorer operation endpoint as the Explorer page, so the change lands in
        the real silo. The write response already carries the matcher's reading of the row. Every test can be reverted.
      </p>
    </div>
    <div class="bento" style="gap:12px;">
      <div class="col-6"><div class="card card-pad-lg" style="height:100%;">
        <p class="eyebrow">Insert · DB1</p>
        <h3 class="h-md" style="margin-top:6px;">A checkout typed with a damaged code</h3>
        <div class="u-two" style="margin-top:10px;">
          <input id="tCode" class="field field-sm mono" value="med asali 0O8" spellcheck="false">
          <select id="tVendor" class="field field-sm u-select"></select>
        </div>
        <div class="u-three">
          <input id="tPrice" class="field field-sm" style="margin-top:10px;" value="85">
          <select id="tMethod" class="field field-sm u-select" style="margin-top:10px;">
            <option value="manual">manual</option><option value="ocr">ocr</option><option value="barcode">barcode</option>
          </select>
          <input id="tDate" class="field field-sm" style="margin-top:10px;" value="2025-04-20 10:15:00">
        </div>
        <div class="row-wrap gap-2" style="margin-top:12px;">
          <button class="btn btn-primary btn-sm" id="btnInsert">Insert into DB1</button>
          <button class="btn btn-ghost btn-sm" id="btnInsertUndo" disabled>Delete it again</button>
        </div>
        <div id="tInsertOut" style="margin-top:12px;"></div>
      </div></div>

      <div class="col-6"><div class="card card-pad-lg" style="height:100%;">

        <h3 class="h-md" style="margin-top:6px;">A counterfeit one edit from a real code</h3>
        <p class="small muted" style="margin-top:6px;">Code <span class="u-code">MED-ASALI-011</span> scanned by barcode at an unlicensed kiosk for Rs 30. String similarity alone would call it Omez or Calcirol.</p>
        <div class="row-wrap gap-2" style="margin-top:12px;">

          <button class="btn btn-ghost btn-sm" id="btnFakeUndo" disabled>Delete it again</button>
        </div>

      </div></div>

      <div class="col-6"><div class="card card-pad-lg" style="height:100%;">
        <p class="eyebrow">Modify · DB3</p>
        <h3 class="h-md" style="margin-top:6px;">Change a product's MRP</h3>
        <p class="small muted" style="margin-top:6px;">Price agreement is evidence. Change the registered MRP of a product and re-run the match for a noisy sale of it.</p>
        <div class="u-two" style="margin-top:10px;">

          <button class="btn btn-ghost btn-sm" id="btnMrpUndo" disabled>Restore</button>

      <div class="col-6"><div class="card card-pad-lg" style="height:100%;">
        <p class="eyebrow">Delete · DB3</p>
        <h3 class="h-md" style="margin-top:6px;">Remove a product from the registry</h3>
        <p class="small muted" style="margin-top:6px;">Its noisy records lose their best candidate. Watch them fall to review or to "no registered product".</p>
        <div class="u-two" style="margin-top:10px;">
